description:
The bit-vector type has no property coverage for the invariants that its whole API depends on. Add property tests for the five invariant families that define correct behaviour.

## Background

The padding invariant is the crate's most load-bearing: bits beyond the logical length must be zero after every mutation, because population count, rank, select, and equality all read the underlying words directly. The other four families are the algebraic ones a reader would expect to hold: double inversion is the identity, a shift one way and back recovers the original, push followed by pop recovers the original, and the butterfly transform is its own inverse.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A property-test module covers padding bits remaining zero after every mutating operation the type exposes.
- [hard] REQ-02: Property tests cover double inversion, shift round trips, push-and-pop round trips, and butterfly self-inversion.
- [hard] REQ-03: Generated lengths span word boundaries, including lengths of zero, one, sixty-three, sixty-four, and sixty-five bits.
- [hard] REQ-04: The padding property fails if tail masking is removed from any constructor, demonstrating that it constrains the invariant rather than restating it.
- [hard] REQ-05: Cases that exceed the fast tier carry a lowercase `slow:` tagged reason, and the fast tier stays inside its per-test and whole-suite budgets.
- [hard] REQ-06: The suite passes, and clippy with warnings denied plus formatting pass.
title: Add property tests for BitVec structural invariants
